title: The Promise of Rosewater Lane
premise: Mirabel Underhill built her life on small, survivable steps: a tiny café on Rosewater Lane, a lease she can barely hold, and a careful distance from the family that once made her feel like too much. When her sister's engagement party forces her home, she hires Theo Marsh—a quiet carpenter who repairs her café's sagging shelves—to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. But the fake date curdles into something real by dessert, and Mirabel must decide whether to accept a prestigious pastry residency in Lyon that would save her career but end whatever is growing between them. In the end, she chooses neither the safe path nor the grand gesture alone: she negotiates a delayed start to the residency, signs a new lease with Theo as her business partner, and learns that belonging isn't something you find—it's something you build, one honest step at a time.
about_author: Xanthe Whitlock is the pen name of a former bakery counter worker who spent six years writing love stories during the slow hours between morning rushes. She lives in a coastal town where every street corner smells faintly of salt and sugar.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A final notice arrives at Rosewater Lane Café the same week her sister texts about the engagement party. Mirabel counts her savings, considers selling her grandmother's recipe book, and rehearses excuses. Emotional beat: quiet desperation masked as competence—the reader sees how fragile her 'safe' life really is.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixed Shelves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo comes to repair water-damaged shelving and notices Mirabel feeding a homeless regular for free. He recognizes a fellow survivor of hard years without naming it. They talk past closing time over burnt shortbread. Emotional beat: cautious recognition—two people who measure safety in small steps sensing a kinship.

chapters.title: An Indecent Proposal, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Cornered by her mother's phone call, Mirabel blurts that she's bringing a boyfriend. Panicked, she asks Theo, offering free repairs labor in trade. He hesitates, then agrees—for reasons he doesn't examine. Emotional beat: comic desperation shading into vulnerability as both admit they dread going home alone.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over two evenings, they build their fake history: how they met, first date, inside jokes. The invented details keep sliding into truths—his mother's illness, her father's disappointment. Emotional beat: intimacy through fabrication; every lie they rehearse reveals something real.

chapters.title: The Underhill Reunion
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The family estate brims with success stories; Mirabel performs happiness while her mother compares her to her surgeon sister. Theo plays his role perfectly—too perfectly—and defends her café when an uncle sneers. Emotional beat: the ache of being unseen in your own family, and the shock of being defended.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At dessert, Mirabel serves a rosewater cake from her grandmother's recipe, and the room goes silent with memory. Her grandmother's old friend embraces her; her mother's eyes soften. Later, on the porch, Theo kisses her—or she kisses him; neither will say who started it. Emotional beat: the fake collapses; grief and longing braid together.

chapters.title: What We Agreed Not to Want
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back home, Theo pulls away, convinced he has nothing to offer someone rebuilding her life. Mirabel misreads it as regret. Meanwhile, the Lyon residency acceptance letter arrives—full scholarship, immediate start. Emotional beat: mutual retreat; both choose old fears over new hope just as opportunity forces a deadline.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her landlord offers the space to a chain bakery unless she can match their offer in ten days. Lyon's start date moves up. Her sister, visiting unannounced, sees the eviction letter and finally understands what Mirabel sacrificed to stay small and safe. Emotional beat: crisis converging—career, love, and home all demand a choice at once.

chapters.title: Rosewater and Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the café's last-chance community night, Mirabel bakes everything she loves; Theo builds her a display case from salvaged wood instead of leaving town. Confronted by her family arriving unexpectedly, she speaks her truth: she was never failing, she was surviving. Emotional beat: climax—Mirabel claims her voice, and Theo stops believing he's temporary.

chapters.title: The Promise of Rosewater Lane
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue-adjacent. Six months later: renegotiated lease signed with Theo as partner, Lyon deferred one year with the chef's blessing, her mother sitting at the counter learning to pipe rosettes. The café thrives not because it's safe, but because it's hers. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging built deliberately, memory honored, survival transformed into home.
